gaps.sentence: Had I ___ the risks, I would never have invested.
gaps.explanation: After inverted 'Had I', the past participle follows: known.

gaps.sentence: You may keep the book provided that you ___ it by Friday.
gaps.explanation: 'Provided that' introduces a condition in the present simple: return.

gaps.sentence: You will not pass the course unless you ___ all the assignments.
gaps.hint: unless means if not, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces a negative condition and takes the present simple: complete.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ more at university!
gaps.explanation: 'If only + past perfect' — regret about a past failure.

gaps.sentence: If the pain ___, stop taking the tablets and call your doctor.
gaps.hint: medical instruction with present after if
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: gets worse.

gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ harder at school when he had the chance.
gaps.hint: past regret, wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect after 'wish': had worked.

gaps.sentence: You can borrow the car provided that you ___ it back by Sunday.
gaps.explanation: 'Provided that' introduces a requirement and takes the present simple: bring.
